brief.meaningEn: Reduce the trust others place in someone after an error or unreliable act.
brief.meaningZh: 因錯誤或不可靠的行為，令別人對某人的信任減弱。
brief.grammar: Pattern: dent/dents/dented/denting + a possessive determiner or noun possessive + credibility (e.g. dent your credibility; dent the guide’s credibility). An error, repeated mistake or unreliable act is often the subject.
brief.register: Neutral to formal professional or community discussion. A colleague, organiser or reviewer can say it to someone assessing how a visible error affects other people's trust.
brief.boundaryZh: 重點是別人對你的可信程度有所下降，不必等同完全失去信任；須有可見的失誤與受影響的對象。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要因任何小瑕疵就斷言信譽已全毀，也不要把 credibility 誤作個人心情。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出哪項失誤令哪些人較難信任說話者，以及可如何修補。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 33, row 2; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: One careless error can dent your credibility.

listening.en: A club secretary sent members the wrong meeting date twice. Even after the correction, some members checked her next notice elsewhere. The repeated errors dented her credibility.
listening.zh: 社團秘書兩次向會員發出錯誤開會日期。即使她已更正，部分會員仍向別處核實下一則通告。反覆失誤損害了她的可信度。
listening.promptZh: dented her credibility 在這裏指甚麼？

options.en: Members trusted her announcements less after the repeated errors.
options.zh: 反覆錯誤後，會員對她的通告較不信任。

options.en: Members forgot the club’s name after the correction.
options.zh: 更正後會員忘記了社團名稱。

options.en: She lost all possibility of ever regaining anyone’s trust.
options.zh: 她永遠不可能重獲任何人的信任。

options.en: The dates became difficult to read because of the notice design.
options.zh: 通告設計令日期難以閱讀。

listening.explanationZh: 有人開始另行核實，顯示信任減弱；dent 不必然表示信任永久完全消失。

reply.promptEn: Why are members checking the secretary’s next notice against another source?
reply.promptZh: （會員為何要另行核實秘書的下一則通告？）

options.en: Her earlier date errors made them less confident in her notices.
options.zh: 她先前的日期錯誤令他們對通告較沒信心。

options.en: They want confirmation because two past notices were wrong.
options.zh: 過去兩則通告有誤，他們想再確認。

options.en: The repeated mistakes dented her credibility with the members.
options.zh: 反覆失誤損害了她在會員心中的可信度。

options.en: They now verify her information before making plans.
options.zh: 他們現在會先核實她的資料，再作安排。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋會員因先前錯誤而較難信任通告；金句明確表達信譽受損。

options.en: The errors dented the guide’s credibility, though the group may still trust future corrected notices.
options.zh: 錯誤損害了導賞員的可信度，但大家仍可能相信之後經核對的通告。

options.en: The group no longer needs directions because it can make a call.
options.zh: 大家能打電話，所以以後都毋須路線指引。

options.en: The guide’s credibility improved simply because the mistakes were repeated.
options.zh: 錯誤重複發生，本身就令導賞員更可信。

scene.explanationZh: 參加者改為先核實，表示信任減弱；題目沒有證明信任已永久消失。
scene.promptZh: 社區導賞員兩次把集合地點寫錯，參加者之後會先致電確認才出門。哪句最貼切？

options.en: An organiser repeatedly gives wrong start times, so people verify each message.
options.zh: 主辦者屢次給錯開始時間，大家因而核實每則訊息。

options.en: A speaker corrects one typo before publication, and no reader ever sees it.
options.zh: 講者在發布前修正一個錯字，沒有讀者看到。

options.en: A seller promises delivery on three dates and misses all three, making customers doubtful.
options.zh: 賣家三次承諾送貨卻都未能兌現，令顧客生疑。

contrast.explanationZh: 未公開的錯字未令任何人對講者的資料失去信任；另兩項已有可見信任下降。
contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不適合說 dent someone’s credibility？

options.en: Those errors may dent your credibility; correct this notice clearly and check the next one before sending it.
options.zh: 那些錯誤可能損害你的可信度；清楚更正這則通告，下一則發出前再核對。

options.en: One more correction guarantees that every parent will trust the next notice without checking.
options.zh: 再更正一次便保證每位家長不用核實也會相信下一則通告。

options.en: The calls prove the parents never valued your work, regardless of the wrong times.
options.zh: 家長來電證明他們一直不重視你的工作，與錯誤時間無關。

dialogue.explanationZh: 家長另行核實顯示信任受影響；回應應承認可能損傷並提出具體修補做法。
dialogue.promptZh: 同事說：「我又把活動時間發錯，家長現在每次都會打電話確認。」你怎樣回應較貼切？

speaking.en: Repeated timetable errors can dent your credibility with the people relying on your updates.
speaking.zh: 時間表反覆出錯，可能損害依賴你更新資訊的人對你的信任。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出甚麼失誤影響哪些人的信任。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區運動會的司庫兩次在捐款報告中列錯總額，令捐款人開始另行核實數字。司庫更正報告，並安排另一人於發布前核對。用一至兩句英文描述對信任的影響及修補方法。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出兩次錯誤總額如何令捐款人較難信任報告，以及更正和第二人發布前核對；不要說信任永遠不可能恢復。

examples.en: The treasurer issued two incorrect donation totals, which dented her credibility with donors; she corrected the report and asked a second person to check future figures before publication.
examples.zh: 司庫兩次公布錯誤捐款總額，損害她在捐款人心中的可信度；她更正報告，並請第二人在日後數字發布前核對。

examples.en: The treasurer’s wrong totals may dent her credibility when donors start checking the figures elsewhere; she corrected the event report and arranged an independent review before its next release.
examples.zh: 捐款人開始另行核實數字，錯誤總額可能損害司庫的可信度；她更正運動會的報告，並安排在下次發布前進行獨立核對。

takeaways.en: A false claim can dent your credibility even if you later correct it.
takeaways.zh: 即使之後更正，錯誤說法仍可能損害你的可信度。

takeaways.en: Checking a figure before publication can prevent it from denting your credibility.
takeaways.zh: 發布前核對數字，可避免它損害你的可信度。

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent English, Chinese, media and QA review remain pending.

brief.meaningEn: A message or its implication causes an immediate emotional hurt.
brief.meaningZh: 話語或其中的暗示令人一時感到難受。
brief.grammar: Pattern: the/that/my/your/his/her/our/their message + can/could/may/might + sting; past the message stung. Message is the subject and sting describes its emotional effect on a listener.
brief.register: Neutral conversational or reflective language. A friend, colleague or teacher may use it when explaining to a listener why particular wording feels hurtful; do not assert the writer's intention.
brief.boundaryZh: 本課重點是某句話當下造成刺痛；與 hurt may run deeper 的持續、較深層傷害不同。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要只因對方反對意見便稱 sting；需指出哪個措辭或暗示令聽者受傷。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出說了甚麼、聽者可能如何理解，以及為何會感到難受。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 33, row 7; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: The message can sting when someone needs support.

listening.en: After Priya volunteered to lead the display, the coordinator wrote, “We need someone more reliable.” Priya had worked on every earlier display, so the message stung.
listening.zh: 普麗雅主動提出帶領展覽布置，協調員卻寫道：「我們需要一個更可靠的人。」她之前每次都參與，這句話令她刺痛。

options.en: It implied Priya was unreliable despite her earlier work.
options.zh: 這句話暗示普麗雅不可靠，儘管她過去一直有幫忙。

options.en: It offered Priya a different role with the same responsibility.
options.zh: 它讓普麗雅擔任責任相同的另一角色。

options.en: It listed the practical tasks needed for the display.
options.zh: 它列出展覽布置所需的實際工作。

options.en: It showed that the coordinator had forgotten the display date.
options.zh: 它顯示協調員忘記了展覽日期。

listening.explanationZh: 「更可靠的人」暗示她不可靠，可能令一直有幫忙的她難受；無須猜測協調員本意。

reply.promptEn: Why did Priya find the coordinator’s reply painful?
reply.promptZh: （普麗雅為何覺得協調員的回覆難受？）

options.en: It suggested her previous effort had not earned trust.
options.zh: 它暗示她過去的努力仍未換來信任。

options.en: She heard “more reliable” as a criticism of her dependability.
options.zh: 她把「更可靠」理解為批評她不可信賴。

options.en: The message stung because it seemed to dismiss her steady work.
options.zh: 那句話令人刺痛，因為它似乎否定她一直以來的付出。

options.en: It left her feeling that her help had been overlooked.
options.zh: 它令她覺得自己的幫忙被忽略。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都由實際措辭解釋她的受傷感；金句用 sting 表達話語造成的即時刺痛。

options.en: The message can sting because it implies the teammate usually holds the group back.
options.zh: 那句話可能令人刺痛，因為它暗示隊友平日常拖累大家。

options.en: The message proves the sender intended to insult the teammate.
options.zh: 那句話證明發訊人有意侮辱隊友。

options.en: The teammate must be upset only about the time the message arrived.
options.zh: 隊友一定只因訊息到達的時間而難過。

scene.explanationZh: 「總算沒有拖累」含有負面暗示，足以使人難受；不應武斷推斷發訊人的意圖。
scene.promptZh: 隊友收到「你這次總算沒有拖累大家」的訊息，雖然表面像稱讚，卻覺得不舒服。哪句最貼切？

options.en: “We need someone more competent this time.”
options.zh: 「這次我們需要一個更有能力的人。」

options.en: “Thank you for helping; could you cover the welcome desk instead?”
options.zh: 「謝謝你幫忙；這次可否轉去接待處？」

options.en: “At least you did not slow us down today.”
options.zh: 「起碼你今天沒有拖慢我們。」

contrast.explanationZh: 感謝對方並提出合理調整，沒有直接否定其能力；另兩句帶有令人刺痛的暗示。
contrast.promptZh: 哪句最不可能因其措辭而 sting 一位曾努力幫忙的義工？

options.en: That message could sting because it makes your earlier effort sound poor; you can ask which parts need improving.
options.zh: 那句話可能令人刺痛，因為它令你之前的努力聽起來很差；你可詢問哪些部分需改善。

options.en: The manager must have meant to hurt you; there is no other possible reading.
options.zh: 經理一定有意傷害你，絕不可能有其他理解。

options.en: You should ignore the wording because it contains the word “better”.
options.zh: 訊息有「較好」一詞，你應完全不理會措辭。

dialogue.explanationZh: 回應承認話語可能造成刺痛，卻不妄猜對方意圖，並提出澄清方法。
dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我花了一週準備，經理卻回覆『這次至少比上次好』。我有點難受。」你怎樣回應較貼切？

speaking.en: The message can sting when it seems to erase someone’s effort.
speaking.zh: 那句話若似乎抹去別人的努力，可能令人刺痛。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出哪個暗示令聽者受傷。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區圖書館的義工努力策劃閱讀活動，卻收到「下次找真正懂書的人吧」的訊息。義工覺得受傷；圖書館主管後來澄清並具體感謝他的工作。用一至兩句英文描述那句話的影響及主管的回應。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出義工做過的努力、訊息中否定能力的暗示、刺痛感，以及主管澄清並具體致謝；不要猜測發訊人本意。

examples.en: The message stung the volunteer who had planned the reading event because “someone who knows books” implied he lacked skill; the manager clarified the remark and thanked him for his work.
examples.zh: 義工努力策劃閱讀活動，那句「真正懂書的人」暗示他沒能力，令他刺痛；主管澄清說法，並感謝他的工作。

examples.en: After the volunteer organised the library session, the message could sting by dismissing his knowledge; the manager explained the wording and thanked him for his careful planning.
examples.zh: 義工籌備圖書館活動後，那句話否定他的知識，可能令他難受；主管解釋措辭，並感謝他細心籌備。

takeaways.en: The message can sting even if its writer intended to offer feedback.
takeaways.zh: 即使發訊者原意是提供意見，那句話仍可能令人刺痛。

takeaways.en: His message stung the volunteer, so the manager explained what was meant.
takeaways.zh: 一句欠周詳的話令義工難受，主管因此解釋原意。

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent English, Chinese, media and QA review remain pending.

brief.meaningEn: Emotional pain may be more substantial or lasting than it first appears.
brief.meaningZh: 情感傷害可能比初看更深、更持久。
brief.grammar: Pattern: (the) hurt + may/might/can/could + run deeper, or the hurt ran deeper; often deeper than + a surface reaction or apology can address. Hurt is the subject.
brief.register: Neutral reflective language about relationships. A friend, counsellor or teammate may say it to another person while cautiously considering why pain or lost trust persists after an apology.
brief.boundaryZh: 本課是深度或持續影響的可能性，不是 2516 某句話當下的刺痛；需有信任或關係仍受影響的線索。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要替當事人斷定永遠不會原諒；may 表示根據後續行為作審慎推測。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出短暫道歉後仍存在甚麼關係或信任問題。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 33, row 10; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: The hurt may run deeper than a quick apology can address.

listening.en: Nora apologised for sharing her friend’s private news. Her friend said “all right” but stopped telling Nora personal things for weeks. The hurt may run deeper than a quick apology can address.
listening.zh: 諾拉為透露朋友的私事道歉。朋友說「好吧」，但之後幾週都不再向她說私事。這份傷害可能比簡短道歉所能處理的更深。
listening.promptZh: 為何說 hurt may run deeper？

options.en: Her friend’s trust may still be affected despite accepting the apology.
options.zh: 朋友雖接受道歉，信任仍可能受影響。

options.en: The apology was longer than the conversation in which the news was shared.
options.zh: 道歉比透露消息時的對話更長。

options.en: Her friend has explicitly said she will never forgive Nora.
options.zh: 朋友已明說永遠不會原諒諾拉。

options.en: The incident had no effect once the word “all right” was spoken.
options.zh: 朋友說了「好吧」，事情便沒有留下任何影響。

listening.explanationZh: 數週不再分享私事，是信任尚未恢復的線索；may 保留不確定性，不推斷永不原諒。

reply.promptEn: Why might Nora need to rebuild trust even after apologising?
reply.promptZh: （諾拉道歉後，為何仍可能需要重建信任？）

options.en: Her friend may still feel uneasy sharing private news.
options.zh: 朋友可能仍不放心分享私事。

options.en: The weeks of silence about personal matters suggest trust has not fully returned.
options.zh: 幾週不再談私事，顯示信任可能尚未完全恢復。

options.en: The hurt may run deeper than a brief apology can address.
options.zh: 傷害可能比簡短道歉所能處理的更深。

options.en: Her continued silence about private matters suggests she may still find it hard to trust Nora.
options.zh: 她持續不談私事，顯示她可能仍難以信任諾拉。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都合理回應為何簡短道歉未必足夠；金句審慎表達較深的傷害。

options.en: The hurt may run deeper because their trust appears to remain strained.
options.zh: 傷害可能比表面更深，因為彼此信任似乎仍有裂痕。

options.en: The apology proves their trust has completely returned.
options.zh: 道歉證明雙方的信任已完全恢復。

options.en: The other person is certain to distrust the teammate forever.
options.zh: 對方必然會永遠不信任隊友。

scene.explanationZh: 後來不再分享紀錄，是信任尚有影響的線索；不可斷言永久不信任。
scene.promptZh: 隊友為未經同意公開另一人的訓練紀錄道歉；對方說理解，之後卻不再把自己的紀錄交給隊友。哪句最貼切？

options.en: A friend accepts an apology but keeps avoiding the subject for months.
options.zh: 朋友接受道歉後，幾個月來仍避談那件事。

options.en: Two friends resolve a minor scheduling mix-up and immediately return to their usual plans without unease.
options.zh: 兩名朋友解決一次小小時間誤會後，毫無芥蒂地恢復原來安排。

options.en: A colleague says the matter is settled but stops sharing ideas with that coworker.
options.zh: 同事說事情已解決，卻不再與那人分享構思。

contrast.explanationZh: 小誤會已解決，且沒有後續不安或信任受損線索；另兩項顯示影響可能持續。
contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不支持說 hurt may run deeper？

options.en: The hurt may run deeper than it looks; give her time and show you will respect her privacy.
options.zh: 傷害可能比表面更深；給她時間，並以行動尊重私隱。

options.en: She said “fine”, so you can assume her trust is fully restored.
options.zh: 她說「沒事」，你便可假設信任已完全恢復。

options.en: Her silence proves she will never want to be friends again.
options.zh: 她沉默證明她永遠不想再做朋友。

dialogue.explanationZh: 不再分享私事提示傷害可能持續，應以尊重和時間修補，而非作絕對斷言。
dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「我已為洩露她的私事道歉，她說沒事，但現在甚麼都不肯跟我說。」你怎樣回應較貼切？

speaking.en: After the apology, the hurt may run deeper if the person still avoids sharing personal news.
speaking.zh: 道歉後若當事人仍避談私事，傷害可能比表面更深。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出甚麼後續行為顯示信任未必恢復。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：樂隊領隊兩次沒有邀請一名成員參加排練，之後道歉。成員說接受，卻在往後幾週不再主動提出獨奏構思；領隊決定尊重對方節奏，逐步重新建立合作信任。用一至兩句英文描述傷害可能比初看更深及可行做法。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出兩次被排除在排練外、成員接受道歉後仍不願提出構思，以及領隊尊重其節奏並逐步重建信任；不要斷言成員永遠不會再參與。

examples.en: The hurt may run deeper than the accepted apology suggests: after being left out of two rehearsals, the musician still holds back solo ideas, so the leader should respect their pace and rebuild trust gradually.
examples.zh: 成員兩次被排除在排練外；即使接受道歉，仍不願提出獨奏構思，傷害可能比表面更深，因此領隊應尊重其節奏，逐步重建信任。

examples.en: Although the musician accepted the apology for two missed rehearsal invitations, the hurt may run deeper because they no longer offer solo ideas; the band leader can give them time and invite them back without pressure.
examples.zh: 樂隊成員接受了兩次未獲邀排練的道歉，但不再提出獨奏構思，傷害可能較深；領隊可給予時間，以不施壓的方式邀請成員重新參與。

takeaways.en: The hurt may run deeper when the same betrayal changes what a friend feels safe sharing.
takeaways.zh: 若同一次背叛令朋友不敢再分享私事，傷害可能比表面更深。

takeaways.en: A quick apology matters, but the hurt may run deeper than words alone can repair.
takeaways.zh: 簡短道歉有其價值，但傷害可能比言語所能修補的更深。

brief.meaningEn: Useful but not guaranteed to work correctly in every case.
brief.meaningZh: 方法或裝置有用，但不能保證每次都奏效。
brief.grammar: Pattern: X is/was not foolproof, often useful but not foolproof. Foolproof is an adjective complement; not negates the claim that a method works in every case.
brief.register: Neutral everyday and professional evaluation. A user, organiser or technician may say it to people relying on a method or device when explaining a realistic failure and backup.
brief.boundaryZh: not foolproof 指非百分百可靠；不要把偶發失敗寫成根本無用，也不要因有用便聲稱永不失靈。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把 foolproof 誤作「只有笨人才用」；它談的是出錯的可能。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出方案的好處、剩餘風險，以及適當後備做法。

sources.sentence: The new lock is useful but not foolproof.

listening.en: The theatre’s online ticket scanner usually moves queues quickly, but a damaged code sometimes will not scan. Staff keep a printed booking list because the scanner is helpful but not foolproof.
listening.zh: 劇院的網上門票掃描器通常能加快排隊，但受損條碼有時掃不到。職員備有列印的預約名單，因為掃描器有用但並非萬無一失。
listening.promptZh: not foolproof 在這裏指甚麼？

options.en: The scanner normally helps but may fail with a damaged code.
options.zh: 掃描器通常有幫助，但遇上受損條碼可能失靈。

options.en: The scanner has never worked for any ticket.
options.zh: 掃描器對任何門票都從未奏效。

options.en: The printed list proves every online booking was wrong.
options.zh: 列印名單證明所有網上預約都有錯。

options.en: A faster queue guarantees that the scanner cannot fail.
options.zh: 隊伍較快便保證掃描器不會失靈。

listening.explanationZh: 裝置通常加快入場，卻有明確失靈情況，故備有名單；不是全然無用或絕不出錯。

reply.promptEn: Why do staff keep a printed booking list if the scanner usually works?
reply.promptZh: （掃描器通常有效，職員為何仍備有列印名單？）

options.en: Damaged codes may need a manual way to confirm bookings.
options.zh: 受損條碼可能需要人手核實預約。

options.en: The list is a backup for the occasional failed scan.
options.zh: 名單可作偶發掃描失敗時的後備。

options.en: The scanner is useful but not foolproof.
options.zh: 掃描器有用，但並非萬無一失。

options.en: Staff can still admit booked visitors when a code cannot be read.
options.zh: 條碼讀不到時，職員仍可讓已預約訪客入場。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說明後備名單能處理偶發失敗；金句概括有用但非百分百可靠。

options.en: The online system is useful but not foolproof, so a paper list is a sensible backup.
options.zh: 網上系統方便卻並非萬無一失，紙本名單是合理後備。

options.en: The system is completely useless because it cannot work without a connection.
options.zh: 系統一旦斷網就不運作，所以完全無用。

options.en: The paper list shows that online bookings can never be trusted.
options.zh: 紙本名單表示網上預約永遠不可信。

scene.explanationZh: 通常方便而斷網時受限，符合有用但非萬無一失；紙本後備不等於全面否定系統。
scene.promptZh: 社區中心用網上報名系統，大多數時候很方便，但斷網時職員須改查紙本名單。哪句最貼切？

options.en: A backup copy is wise because a device may occasionally fail.
options.zh: 裝置偶爾可能失靈，所以備份明智。

options.en: The method is guaranteed to work perfectly every time without exception.
options.zh: 這方法保證每次都完美奏效，絕無例外。

options.en: The plan works in most cases, but rare conditions still need a fallback.
options.zh: 計劃多數情況有效，但罕見情況仍需後備。

contrast.explanationZh: 保證百分百成功正與 not foolproof 相反。
contrast.promptZh: 哪個說法最不符合 not foolproof？

options.en: It is helpful but not foolproof; let us keep a manual attendance option for those cases.
options.zh: 它有幫助但並非萬無一失；我們應保留人手點名供這類情況使用。

options.en: Because it saves time, students with dead phones can simply be marked absent.
options.zh: 它既然省時，手機沒電的學生便可直接記作缺席。

options.en: One missed scan means we should abandon every digital tool in school.
options.zh: 一次掃碼失敗表示學校應停用所有電子工具。

dialogue.explanationZh: 承認效率，同時為可預見失敗設後備；其餘兩項忽略學生或把局部問題推得過遠。
dialogue.promptZh: 同事說：「這個自動點名系統很省時；但手機沒電的學生偶爾無法掃碼。」你怎樣回應最貼切？

speaking.en: The attendance app is convenient but not foolproof when a student’s phone has no power.
speaking.zh: 點名程式方便，但學生手機沒電時就並非萬無一失。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出哪種例外需要後備方法。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：學校考試室用電子鐘同步時間，大部分日子很準；停電時可能停止運作，因此主任準備一個電池時鐘。用一至兩句英文說明好處、風險和後備。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出電子鐘通常準確、停電時可能停下，以及電池鐘作後備；不要說電子鐘完全無用或絕不會失靈。

examples.en: The synchronised clock is accurate most days but not foolproof during a power cut, so the exam officer keeps a battery clock as backup.
examples.zh: 同步電子鐘平日準確，但停電時並非萬無一失；考試主任因此備有電池鐘作後備。

examples.en: Because the electronic clock could stop if power fails, it is not foolproof despite usually keeping good time; a battery clock protects the exam schedule.
examples.zh: 電子鐘通常準時，但停電時可能停下，因此並非萬無一失；電池鐘可保障考試時間安排。

takeaways.en: A useful map app is not foolproof when a road closes without warning.
takeaways.zh: 地圖程式有用，但道路突然封閉時也並非萬無一失。

takeaways.en: The reminder system is not foolproof, so a second person checks important deadlines.
takeaways.zh: 提醒系統並非萬無一失，因此由第二人核對重要期限。
